deltas.delta: Three single web3_clientVersion requests on 2026-11-24 returned op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown twice and op-reth/v2.8.1-72207294 once, behind one load balancer cookie and proxyd. The string 0.0.0-dev with commit unknown is the fallback of the op-version crate when GIT_VERSION and GIT_COMMIT are not set at build time (rust/op-version/src/lib.rs lines 3-7 and 19-22), and that crate and its use in op-reth/bin/src/main.rs are present at op-reth/v2.8.1, v2.9.0, v2.10.0-rc.1 and develop, so the string names no revision.

Every published revision from op-reth/v2.8.2 to develop on 2026-11-24 pins the same execution stack: ruint 1.20.0, revm 43.0.3, revm-interpreter 43.0.2, op-revm 20.0.0, alloy-primitives 1.7.3, fixed-cache 0.1.10 and rapidhash 4.4.1 (v2.8.1 differs only by revm 43.0.2 and revm-interpreter 43.0.1). A dev build cut from any of them runs the arithmetic, jump and hashing code already read.

op-revm in the optimism tree builds its EVM with EthInstructions::new_mainnet_with_spec (rust/op-revm/src/evm.rs line 38 at op-reth/v2.9.0 and v2.10.0-rc.1), and alloy-op-evm types the EVM with EthInstructions (rust/alloy-op-evm/src/lib.rs lines 63, 114, 139, 171). No instruction is replaced for OP chains.

cleared.check: The four Ink swaps in pool 0x69b7ffdbaba1b2f0c4984cbe6c0823a609de9cbce5247cea64fff9eb70fefe2f that replay.py reported as not reproduced: was the step that ends at tick 276390 a wrong bitmap search on the node.
cleared.result: No. The swap call in the trace names tick spacing 90 and no hook. From tick 276324 the compressed tick is 3070, the search starts at 3071, which is bit 255 of word 11, so nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord returns 276390 uninitialized and the loop takes a second step with unchanged liquidity. Bitmap word 11 for spacing 90 has no bit at position 255, and storage shows no initialized tick between 276300 and 276500 at block 62031730. That is the specified behaviour of TickBitmap.sol and Pool.sol, and the replay with spacing 90 matches price, tick, liquidity and both amounts.

cleared.check: Does op-revm or alloy-op-evm, as pinned by op-reth v2.9.0 and v2.10.0-rc.1, replace any EVM instruction.
cleared.result: No. rust/op-revm/src/evm.rs line 38 builds EthInstructions::new_mainnet_with_spec and alloy-op-evm lib.rs types every OP EVM with EthInstructions. OP chains differ from Ethereum in the handler (L1 and operator fees, deposits) and in precompiles, not in opcode semantics. Base was read in cycle 10 and World Chain and Zora link the same op-revm 20.0.0.

cleared.check: fixed-cache 0.1.11 (published 2026-10-19): does its change to the lock protocol alter what the keccak cache returns, and does any client of the seven chains pin it.
cleared.result: No client pins it: op-reth v2.8.2, v2.9.0, v2.10.0-rc.1 and develop, Base main, World Chain main, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 and reth main all pin 0.1.10. The release adds an opt-in seqlock read path (LOCK_FREE_READS, default DISABLED, unsafe to enable), a version counter in the top 8 bits of the bucket tag, and makes try_lock_ret compare tags without those bits. In the default path a tag match is still followed by key.equivalent, and alloy-primitives 1.7.3 compares the full input slice (keccak_cache.rs Key::eq), so fewer tag bits only add key comparisons. alloy-primitives 1.7.3 sets only STATS and EPOCHS in its CacheConfig, so a client that moved to 0.1.11 would run the locked path. Also Key holds MaybeUninit bytes, which the lock-free path forbids, so turning it on in alloy would be unsound and needs a reread.

cleared.check: Which block producing code could run a different EVM path than the public endpoint: external builders behind rollup-boost, and the fault proof programs.
cleared.result: A builder block is validated with engine_newPayload on the sequencer's own execution client before use and replaced by the local block if invalid, and every node re-executes it, so a builder that computed differently produces a rejected block and no state. The kona proof program had three derivation faults fixed by 26 March 2026, at a time when it was only the fallback proof system. Fault proofs govern L1 withdrawals, not the PoolManager balance, and acting on a fault needs the proposer or batcher, actor operator.

cleared.check: Known weaknesses of the last two years not settled in cycle 10: the reth and op-reth state root fault of 5 November 2026 (fixed in op-reth v2.8.1 and Base node-reth v1.5.3), the kona fallback proof faults, the ruint advisories.
cleared.result: The state root fault lets a crafted transaction make the legacy state root code, which OP Stack block builders used, return a wrong root, so nodes disagree on the block and processing stalls. It does not change an opcode result or a storage value the PoolManager reads, the report states that L2 withdrawals were unaffected, and the endpoints run op-reth v2.8.1 or later and Base v1.5.6. An ordinary account could at most delay blocks, which takes no funds. The other items are answered above. None gives an ordinary account a path to PoolManager funds.

leads.why: A builder that differs from the sequencer client only produces rejected blocks, so this is a liveness question, unless a chain runs rollup-boost without validation.

leadResults.answer: The endpoint still balances between op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown and op-reth/v2.8.1-72207294. The dev string is the op-version fallback for a build without GIT_VERSION and GIT_COMMIT, present at every op-reth tag from v2.8.1 to develop, and all those revisions pin ruint 1.20.0, revm-interpreter 43.0.2 (43.0.1 at v2.8.1), op-revm 20.0.0, alloy-primitives 1.7.3 and fixed-cache 0.1.10. With web3_clientVersion before and after each request in one batch, 73,329 battery and targeted vectors, 248 of 250 pmdiff scripts and 71,118 keccak bucket words were bracketed by the dev build alone and all matched, as did every other request. Because proxyd can send members of one batch to different backends, bracketing is strong evidence and not proof of which backend ran each eth_call.

fixed-cache 0.1.11 adds an opt-in lock-free read path (LOCK_FREE_READS, default DISABLED), a version counter in the top 8 tag bits, and makes the tag comparison in try_lock_ret ignore those bits. In the default locked path a tag match is still followed by full key equality, so the cache cannot return the hash of another input. alloy-primitives 1.7.3, the newest release, does not enable lock-free reads. No client of the seven chains pins 0.1.11: op-reth up to v2.10.0-rc.1 and develop, Base main, World Chain main, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 and reth main all pin 0.1.10. The closed mega-reth was not readable.

The public build files of conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 build with the cache off: keccak-cache-global is opt-in in crates/bin and crates/node, no dependency enables it, and docker-bake.hcl passes no FEATURES argument to the Dockerfile. Whether Conduit's private pipeline passes it is not public. Both cases are safe as read: with the feature on, the lockfile pins alloy-primitives 1.7.3 and fixed-cache 0.1.10, the text cycle 11 cleared.

Building a Rust harness against the rapidhash 4.4.1 crate was refused by the session's permission check again, so the Python transcription is still not compared with compiled code, and the crate has no known-answer vectors for the micro variant with AVALANCHE off. The safety of the cache does not rest on it: alloy's Key compares the whole input after every tag match.
